title: Zero-section and constant-family identifications for specialization
statement:
Use the specialization datum of [def-trf-deformation-specialization], the finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and the Rees deformation of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry]. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be any closed subscheme, and let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Then $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor dimension, and the canonical base-change map on the zero section $z:Z\hookrightarrow N_{Z/X}$ is an isomorphism
$$z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*M.$$

For a constant lift $T_D$ of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, the nearby-cycle unit $M\to\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}M$ is an isomorphism, and the specialization map on $\operatorname{Hom}(A_T,\omega_T)$ is the identity. More generally, if a lift $\widetilde T$ has a closed immersion $T_D\hookrightarrow\widetilde T$ over $T_D$, identical on the generic fibre and inducing an isomorphism on reductions, its Borel--Moore specialization map is an isomorphism, identified with that constant-family identity through invariance of the small etale site under nilpotent thickenings of these Noetherian $D$-schemes.

source.place: Proposition 1.4.2 (equation (1.8)); Example 1.3.3(a)--(b); reduction argument in the proof of Theorem 2.1.3(b)

proof.text: Pass to the etale representative $M'$ of $M$ by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. The two directions of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] give $M'$ the same finite Tor interval and transfer an etale finite-Tor output back to the pro-etale category. The Rees lift is separated finite type over $D$, and its fibres and zero section are exactly those asserted by [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry]. Apply [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange] to this lift and the generic pullback of $M'$: the output is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Thus the preservation assertion follows on the category specified by [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. From now through Step 9 work on the etale site; all comparison maps are the specified maps, so the resulting isomorphisms transfer back. We prove the zero-section comparison as an isomorphism on all bounded constructible etale inputs, a slightly stronger auxiliary assertion needed for truncations.

First establish the constant-family unit without using the zero-section theorem. Put $E_T(L)=\operatorname{Cone}(L\to\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}L)$, taking the cone on functorial derived models. Nearby-cycle exactness and unit compatibility in [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange] make this a triangulated defect functor. For proper $h:T'\to T$, proper base change for $h_D$ identifies $E_T(Rh_*L)$ with $Rh_*E_{T'}(L)$; for smooth $h$, smooth base change identifies $E_{T'}(h^*L)$ with $h^*E_T(L)$. These are comparisons of the unit maps, not merely comparisons of objects. On a geometric point the nearby-cycle unit is the identity: the geometric generic point has trivial small etale topos, so the stalk computation $i^*Rj_*L_{\bar\eta}=L$ has no positive cohomology. On a smooth scheme, a constant finite module therefore has zero defect by smooth base change from that point. A locally constant finite sheaf has zero defect by an etale trivializing cover and the same smooth exchange. For a bounded complex whose cohomology is locally constant, its finite truncation triangles and exactness give the same conclusion. The definition [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] implies that every bounded constructible complex on affine space has such locally constant cohomology on some dense open subset: discard the closures of the finitely many nondense strata for the finitely many cohomology sheaves. Hence $E_{\mathbf A^n}(L)$ vanishes on a dense open.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5, definition of the constant-family defect and its generic vanishing

proof.text: Prove $E_T=0$ by induction on affine ambient dimension. Zariski locality follows from smooth exchange for open immersions. A finite-type affine scheme has a closed immersion into some $\mathbf A^n$; proper exchange for this immersion and closed direct image, exact by [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] and faithful because the counit $i^*Ri_*\simeq\operatorname{id}$ is invertible by [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], reduce to affine space. The case $n=0$ was computed in Step 2. For $n>0$, let $Y$ be the reduced closure of the cohomological support of $E_{\mathbf A^n}(L)$, a proper closed subset by Step 2. Choose a nonzero polynomial $P$ vanishing on $Y$ and a direction $v$ on which its highest homogeneous part is nonzero; such a direction exists because $k$ is infinite. After a linear coordinate change and scalar division, $P$ is monic in the coordinate along $v$. Consequently projection $q:\mathbf A^n\to\mathbf A^{n-1}$ is finite on $Y$: its coordinate ring is a quotient of the algebra generated by that coordinate satisfying the monic equation. In the compactification $\bar q:\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf A^{n-1}\to\mathbf A^{n-1}$, the homogenized monic equation has value $1$ at infinity, so the closure of $Y$ stays in $\mathbf A^n$. Extend $L$ by zero to $\bar L$. The projection $\bar q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]; [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] makes $R\bar q_*\bar L$ bounded constructible (all schemes here are finite type over $k$ and the order of $A$ is invertible). Proper exchange and induction give $R\bar q_*E(\bar L)=E_{\mathbf A^{n-1}}(R\bar q_*\bar L)=0$. On the affine chart its defect is supported on $Y$, and elsewhere only on the infinity section. Their disjoint union is finite over $\mathbf A^{n-1}$. Localization [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] identifies the defect with closed direct image from this finite support. The finite-stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] together with exact geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] makes direct image from a finite scheme exact and conservative: its stalk is the finite product of the input stalks, so a zero product forces every input stalk to vanish, and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] detects zero sheaves. Thus $E(\bar L)=0$ and its restriction $E_{\mathbf A^n}(L)=0$. This closes the induction and proves that the canonical unit $L\to\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}L$ is an isomorphism for every bounded constructible etale $L$.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5, final sentence, with the finite-projection induction of §3.2.4 written out

proof.text:
Using the constant-family unit just proved, define $C_{X,Z}(L)=\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_{X,Z,L})$ where $\gamma:z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}L\to\operatorname{sp}_{Z_D}i^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*L$ is the map of equation (1.8); the last arrow is the inverse unit. These functorial model cones are exact by [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange]. We need its proper/smooth comparison for a morphism $h:X'\to X$ and $Z'=h^{-1}Z$. The geometry node gives a closed immersion from the Rees lift of $(X',Z')$ into $\widetilde X_Z\times_X X'$, so the lifted $h$ is proper if $h$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. If $h$ is flat, tensoring the inclusion $R[t,I/t]\subset R[t,t^{-1}]$ with the flat coordinate algebra $R'$ remains injective by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]; its image is exactly $R'[t,IR'/t]$ since both algebras are generated by $R'[t]$ and the same elements $f/t$. Thus in the flat case the closed immersion is an isomorphism. In particular a smooth $h$ has smooth lift, by smooth base change [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. Its inverse-image zero section is $Z'$ by the geometry node. Nearby-cycle proper/smooth exchange, and ordinary proper/smooth base change on the special fibres in [prop-functor-package], therefore identify the maps $\gamma$, and hence their cones, as
$$C_{X,Z}(Rh_*L')\simeq Rh_{Z*}C_{X',Z'}(L')\quad(h\text{ proper}),\qquad C_{X',Z'}(h^*L)\simeq h_Z^*C_{X,Z}(L)\quad(h\text{ smooth}).$$
Compatibility with the maps follows from the composition/unit compatibility in the nearby-cycle node. This verifies Lemma 3.2.1 on the actual Rees lifts, rather than presupposing smoothness for an arbitrary normal cone.

If $Z=X$, its ideal is zero, so its Rees deformation is the constant family $X_D$ and $\gamma$ is the inverse unit of Step 3, hence $C_{X,X}=0$. Apply proper comparison from Step 4 to the closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ (proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]) to obtain $C_{X,Z}(i_*i^*L)=0$. The localization triangle of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] and exactness of $C$ then identify $C_{X,Z}(j_!j^*L)$ with $C_{X,Z}(L)$, where $j:X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$. Thus it suffices to prove $C=0$ when $i^*L=0$. For $Z=\varnothing$, the target category on $Z$ is zero and the assertion is immediate.

Let $b:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_Z X\to X$ and $Z'=b^{-1}Z$. The ideal of $Z$ is finite type because $X$ is Noetherian; [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] makes $b$ proper, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies its complement with $X\setminus Z$, and [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] makes $Z'$ an effective Cartier divisor. Because $i^*L=0$, the unit $L\to Rb_*b^*L$ is an isomorphism: outside $Z$ it is the identity under that complement isomorphism, and over $Z$ proper base change in [prop-functor-package] gives zero, since $b^*L$ restricts to zero on $Z'$. Exactness [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and conservativity of geometric stalks check the isomorphism. Step 4 consequently reduces the desired vanishing to $(X',Z',b^*L)$. We may hence assume that $Z$ is Cartier. By Zariski locality, choose an affine chart $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ where $Z=V(f)$ is principal. If $B$ is generated over $k$ by $b_1,\ldots,b_r$, the surjection $k[x_1,\ldots,x_r,y]\to B$ sending $y$ to $f$ gives a closed immersion $e:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{r+1}$ whose inverse image of the hyperplane $H=V(y)$ is exactly $Z$, including its nonreduced structure. Closed direct image is exact by [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] and faithful by applying the invertible closed counit of [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]; applying proper comparison to $e$ reduces the assertion to $(\mathbf A^{r+1},H,e_*L)$. Thus it suffices to handle affine space with a coordinate hyperplane.

We prove $C_{\mathbf A^n,H}(L)=0$ for $H=\mathbf A^{n-1}\times\{0\}$ by induction on $n\geq1$, with all bounded constructible inputs. Step 5 reduces the input to $L|_H=0$. Apply the explicit affine-space coordinate-hyperplane case of [lem-trf-dnc-generic-zero-section-vanishing]. Since the target $L|_H$ is zero, its assertion says precisely that $C_{\mathbf A^n,H}(L)$ has zero stalk at every generic point of $H$ (a shift of the specialized restriction does not affect vanishing). Its bounded constructibility implies that the closure $Y$ of its cohomological support is a proper closed subset of $H$. For $n=1$, $H$ is a point and its sole point is generic, so this already proves vanishing and starts the induction.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3 and the base case of §3.2.4

proof.text:
For $n>1$, choose a nonzero polynomial on $H\simeq\mathbf A^{n-1}$ vanishing on $Y$ and a direction $l\subset H$ at which its highest homogeneous part is nonzero. As in Step 3, after coordinates along $l$ the polynomial is monic, so $q|_Y:Y\to H/l$ is finite and the closure of $Y$ in the relative projective-line compactification has no point at infinity. Put $X'=\mathbf A^n/l\simeq\mathbf A^{n-1}$, $Z'=H/l\simeq\mathbf A^{n-2}$ and compactify $q:\mathbf A^n\to X'$ by $\bar q:\bar X=\mathbf P^1\times X'\to X'$; let $\bar Z=\bar q^{-1}Z'$ and extend $L$ by zero to $\bar L$. The projection is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Step 4 and the induction hypothesis give
$$R\bar q_{Z*}C_{\bar X,\bar Z}(\bar L)=C_{X',Z'}(R\bar q_*\bar L)=0.$$
Indeed $(X',Z')$ is the affine hyperplane pair in dimension $n-1$, and its input is bounded constructible by [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility], whose finite-ring and invertibility hypotheses hold for $A=A_{E,n}$. On the affine chart the defect restricts to $C_{\mathbf A^n,H}(L)$, supported on $Y$; elsewhere it is supported on the infinity section over $Z'$. These two disjoint closed subsets form a finite scheme over $Z'$ (use their reduced structures), so by [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] the defect is closed direct image from their union. The finite-stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] , exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], and geometric-stalk conservativity then make $R\bar q_{Z*}$ conservative on such supported complexes, exactly as in Step 3. Hence the defect is zero. This closes the induction. Steps 5--6 reduce every closed pair to it, proving $\gamma_{X,Z,M}$ is the isomorphism claimed in equation (1.8), on the original finite coefficient category by Step 1.

source.place: §3.2.4, completion of Verdier zero-section theorem, including the support/finite-projection argument

proof.text:
For the constant lift, write $\theta_L:L\to\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}L$ for the canonical unit, proved invertible in Step 3. Write $b:\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}\omega_T\to\omega_T$ for the exceptional exchange in the definition [def-trf-deformation-specialization], including the inverse constant-family comparison on the base point. Compatibility of ordinary exchange with the units, and of exceptional exchange with its adjoint mate, in [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange] gives $b\theta_{\omega_T}=1_{\omega_T}$: taking the mate of the ordinary unit square yields this equality by the adjunction triangle equations. The special-fibre composition/adjunction identifications are those of [prop-functor-package]. For $\alpha:A_T\to\omega_T$, naturality of $\theta$ gives $\operatorname{sp}(\alpha)\theta_{A_T}=\theta_{\omega_T}\alpha$. Consequently the defining Borel--Moore specialization is
$$b\,\operatorname{sp}(\alpha)\,\theta_{A_T}=b\theta_{\omega_T}\alpha=\alpha.$$
This proves the identity for the specified canonical map, with no properness assumption on $T$, and transfers to the finite-Tor pro-etale realization by Step 1.

source.place: Examples 1.3.3(a)--(b), with the constant-family unit established independently in Steps 2--3

proof.text:
Let $r:T_D\hookrightarrow\widetilde T$ be the closed immersion in the final clause, and write $r_0:T\hookrightarrow\widetilde T_0$. Since $r$ induces an isomorphism on reductions, it is surjective on underlying sets, so [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism] makes $r$ a finite universal homeomorphism, and every base change of $r$ (to $D^{\rm sh}$, to the geometric generic fibre, and to the special fibre, giving $r_0$) is again a surjective closed immersion, hence by the same lemma a finite universal homeomorphism. Topological invariance of the etale site [lemma-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-site-equivalence] and the resulting equivalence of small etale topoi [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos] apply to these total $D$-schemes; no finite-type-over-$k$ theorem is applied to them. Their etale equivalences identify $i^*Rj_*$ and the nearby-cycle units, since on the generic fibre $r$ is the prescribed identity. The closed immersion $r$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Equivalently, the proper exchange for $r$ in [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange] gives $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}L\simeq Rr_{0*}\operatorname{sp}_{T_D}L$, compatibly with the exchange maps and their adjoint mates. On special fibres, [i-topology] makes $r_0^*$ and $Rr_{0*}=Rr_{0!}$ inverse equivalences. In particular the right adjoint $r_0^!$ of $Rr_{0!}$ is the same quasi-inverse, and [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] identifies $r_0^!\omega_{\widetilde T_0}$ with $\omega_T$. The defining Borel--Moore composite is therefore the constant-family composite followed by the equivalence-induced map
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A_T,\omega_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(A_{\widetilde T_0},\omega_{\widetilde T_0}).$$
The latter is given by the invertible unit $A_{\widetilde T_0}\to Rr_{0*}A_T$ and the invertible exceptional counit $Rr_{0!}r_0^!\omega_{\widetilde T_0}\to\omega_{\widetilde T_0}$. By Step 9 the first composite is the identity, so this proves the final specialization isomorphism and its claimed identification through reduction. The same equivalence has a pro-etale realization, exactly [i-topology], so no coefficient categories have been silently identified.
